Calibration

class Calibration(camera_description, camera_id, camera_position, camera_width, camera_height, camera_max_fps, camera_min_fps, screen_manufacturer, screen_model, screen_position, screen_serial_number, screen_width, screen_height, screen_available_width, screen_available_height, screen_pos_x, screen_pos_y, content_width, content_height, content_width_ratio, content_height_ratio, content_proportion, calibration_date, calibration_hour)[source]

Bases: object

Camera, screen and projected content calibration data.

Attributes:
camera_descriptionstr

Camera description.

camera_idstr

Camera identifier.

camera_positionint

Camera position (index).

camera_width, camera_heightint

Camera resolution in pixels.

camera_max_fps, camera_min_fpsint

Camera frame rate range.

screen_manufacturer, screen_modelstr

Manufacturer and model of the projection screen.

screen_positionint

Screen position (index).

screen_serial_numberstr

Screen serial number.

screen_width, screen_heightint

Screen resolution in pixels.

screen_available_width, screen_available_heightint

Available screen area in pixels.

screen_pos_x, screen_pos_yint

Screen position on the virtual desktop, in pixels.

content_width, content_heightint

Area available for the projection, in pixels.

content_width_ratio, content_height_ratioint

Aspect ratio of the content, e.g. 16 and 9.

content_proportionstr

Aspect ratio name, "4:3" or "16:9".

calibration_date, calibration_hourstr

Date and time of the calibration.

PROPERTIESlist[str], class attribute

Field names, filled by initialize_reflexive.

DATA_PROPERTIESlist, class attribute

Field defaults, filled by initialize_reflexive.

ID_VALUEint, class attribute

Fixed identifier of the single calibration record (1).

PROPORTIONSdict[str, tuple[int, int]], class attribute

Supported aspect ratios by name.

SECTIONS_MAPdict[str, str], class attribute

Field name prefix to .ini section.

IGNORED_PROPERTIESlist[str], class attribute

Class attribute names that must not be saved.

Notes

Every field is required by the constructor; there are no defaults.

Examples

>>> c = Calibration(*[None] * len(Calibration.PROPERTIES))
>>> c.is_valid()
False
>>> c.get_section_for_property("camera_width")
'camera'
>>> c.get_proportion_tuple("16:9")
(16, 9)

is_valid()[source]

Check that no field is None.

Returns:
bool

False if any field of PROPERTIES is None, True otherwise.

set_data(data)[source]

Update the fields from a dictionary.

Parameters:
datadict

Values keyed by field name. Keys that are not fields are ignored, and fields missing from data keep their value.

Notes

No validation or type conversion is done.

get_data()[source]

Return the field values as a one-item list.

Returns:
list[dict]

A list with one dictionary that maps each name of PROPERTIES to its current value.

Return the (width, height) ratio of a proportion name.

Parameters:
proportionstr

Proportion name, "4:3" or "16:9".

Returns:
tuple[int, int]

The ratio from PROPORTIONS, or (0, 0) if the name is unknown.

get_section_for_property(prop_name)[source]

Return the .ini section of a field, based on its prefix.

Parameters:
prop_namestr

Field name.

Returns:
str

Section from SECTIONS_MAP for the first matching prefix, or "geral" if no prefix matches.
